_comment: まんが「空気を 読むって なに？」の 10ページ（content/manga/kuuki_manga.json・size:"page"・speechInImage:true）。形は 連絡の まんが（renraku_manga_v2.json）に そろえた。焼く 字は セリフと 一字一句 同じ（教材データの bakedText）。ふりがなは 教材の 読み辞書から bakedReadings（src/lib/manga-baked.ts）で 出した もの。noText の 前半は RUBY_LETTERING（src/lib/manga-prompt.ts）の 逐語。参照は ヘンディの 設定画と「あなた」の 設定画（scripts/images/kuuki_anata_sheet.json で 作った もの）＋1枚目（p01）が 絵柄アンカー。場面は 2026-10-16 に ユーザーが 選んだ もの（6・7ページは「段ボールを 持った 先輩と ドア」）。失敗の 例は 読む 人（あなた）の 選択として 描き、名前の ある 人物には させない。2026-10-16: 最初の 版は 各ページに output が 無く、gen_images の 既定「landscape illustration, 1024x1536」が 渡って 横長で 描かれ 縦に 引き伸ばされた。いったん 横長の 元絵を 置いたが、ユーザーの 指定「普通の漫画と同じ縦長がいい」で 縦長（1024x1536）で 撮り直した。各 scene に output を 書いて ある。
style: A full-colour Japanese manga PAGE for a language-learning lesson — one portrait page, drawn like a modern colour manga / webtoon: clean confident black linework, soft cel shading, bright friendly palette of sky blue, cream and coral, rounded shapes, no harsh shadows. Light, funny, slightly surreal gag-manga comedy — exaggerated but friendly reactions (sweat drops, little sparkles, a small grey rain cloud over an awkward person), never scary. The page is divided into full-width horizontal panels stacked from top to bottom, separated by white gutters, each panel with a thin black border. People are real human beings with natural proportions, warm friendly faces and exactly five fingers on each hand. Keep every character's face, hair and outfit exactly as in the reference model sheets (Hendy: navy suit and navy necktie, short black hair; YOU: chin-length black bob, warm light-brown skin, bright red open zip-up jacket over a white T-shirt). Other people (customers, tourists, the senior colleague) are ordinary friendly people who do not look like Hendy or YOU. Speech balloons are white, rounded, with a tail pointing at the speaker and never covering a face. Narration captions are white rectangular boxes with a thin black border. Thought bubbles are cloud-shaped with small trailing circles.
noText: Lettering — read this part carefully. All lettering is HORIZONTAL (left to right, yokogaki) — never vertical. Copy every text EXACTLY as given, character for character: do not translate, rephrase, shorten, or add anything. Directly above EVERY kanji, print its reading in small hiragana (furigana), centred over that kanji, clearly separated from it, at about 45% of the kanji height. Use exactly the readings listed below — never guess a reading. Hiragana, katakana, Latin letters, digits and symbols take no furigana. Letter it large and clearly legible in a plain rounded manga font. The picture contains ONLY the texts listed for this page, and no other writing at all: no extra words, no names on shirts, no logos, no watermarks, no signatures, no page numbers, no sound effects other than those listed.
negative: Never: signs, menus, noren curtains, posters, boxes or screens with any writing (leave them blank or use simple pictures), extra spaces inside a word, any Japanese sentence that is not in the list for this page, vertical text, missing furigana over any kanji, furigana over hiragana or katakana, a reading different from the list, misspelled or invented characters, extra words, English translations, photo-realistic rendering, harsh shadows, extra or merged fingers, distorted hands, dark or scary mood, angry or crying faces, real company logos, national flags, tiny unreadable text, panels read right-to-left.

Panel 1 (large): a review board with four small rounded framed pictures in a 2-by-2 grid, each a mini version of an earlier scene, with its label under it: top-left — the ramen counter with YOU (the young new-hire with a chin-length black bob, warm light-brown skin, bright red open zip-up jacket over a white T-shirt, from the second reference sheet) in the middle and the two friends (two young men: one with short black hair in a dark-green hoodie, one with brown hair in a cream shirt; both carry black backpacks) at the entrance, label TEXT A; top-right — the two tourist friends (two young women: the photographer has long brown hair, a cream blouse and a black backpack; the posing friend has long light-brown hair with sunglasses on her head, a white blouse and a blue floral skirt) waiting with the camera, label TEXT B; bottom-left — YOU holding the office door open for the senior colleague (a Japanese woman in her thirties with a short brown ponytail, a light-blue blouse and navy trousers — she does not look like YOU) carrying the cardboard boxes, label TEXT C; bottom-right — YOU kindly asking the same senior colleague (short brown ponytail, light-blue blouse) who has an empty curry plate, label TEXT D. Every mini picture shows the SAME people as on the earlier pages — no new or older people, no glasses on the senior colleague.
Panel 2: Hendy (the PM man in the navy suit and navy necktie, short black hair, from the reference sheet) points at YOU's bright red jacket with a big friendly smile. YOU look down at their own red jacket, surprised and happy. Speech balloon from Hendy: TEXT E.
Panel 3: YOU hold up a smartphone whose screen shows a very simple game picture: a plain white background with a few simple round-headed white figures and ONE red figure (no words on the screen). YOU look excited and ready; Hendy gives a friendly thumbs-up. Speech balloon from Hendy: TEXT F.
Texts on this page — copy each one EXACTLY, character for character, including spaces, punctuation, 「」 brackets, ❌ ⭕ marks, ① ② ③ and digits:
TEXT A — a narration caption box:
    ① 見る
TEXT B — a narration caption box:
    ② 気づく
TEXT C — a narration caption box:
    ③ 動く
TEXT D — a narration caption box:
    分からない ときは 聞く
TEXT E — Hendy's speech balloon:
    この あとの ゲームでは、あなたは 赤い 人です。
TEXT F — Hendy's speech balloon:
    赤い ものだけ 動かせます。何も しない ほうが いい ときも あります。
Furigana readings for the kanji on this page (kanji → hiragana): 見 → み / 気 → き / 動 → うご / 分 → わ / 聞 → き / 赤 → あか / 人 → ひと / 何 → なに
For a word of several kanji, spread its reading over the whole word, each part directly above its own kanji.
EVERY kanji on this page needs its furigana — also a kanji right after 「 brackets or after digits, and a kanji that appears a second time. Before finishing, check each text line by line: no kanji may be left without furigana.
